cards.explanation: The answer is to his own town. Luke says "…everyone went to his own town to register." (Luke 2:3) No one big gathering place, just people heading to their own towns. I think a LOT of people were packing a bag at the same time.

The answer is David. Luke says Joseph "…was from the house and line of David." (Luke 2:4) That's why Bethlehem, the city of David, is where he has to go. His family roots are pointing him down the road, friends.
The answer is False. The text says "While they were there, the time came for her Child to be born." (Luke 2:6) They were still in Bethlehem when it happened. The baby arrived away from home.
The answer is in a manger. Luke says Mary "…laid Him in a manger…" (Luke 2:7) A manger is a feeding trough for animals. Not what you'd pick for a newborn, but that's what the text says.

The answer is that there was no room for them in the inn. Mary laid Him in a manger "…because there was no room for them in the inn." (Luke 2:7) The text says nothing more about why, so I won't guess. I think anyone who has ever shown up somewhere with no room left knows that sinking feeling.

The answer is an angel of the Lord. Luke says "…an angel of the Lord stood before them…" (Luke 2:9) Right there in the field, in the middle of the night shift. Those shepherds clocked in for an ordinary night and got a visitor from heaven, friends.
The answer is terrified. Luke says "…they were terrified." (Luke 2:9) An angel appears and the glory of the Lord shines around them. I think I'd have dropped my whole tray of cookies.

The answer is False. The angel says it is "…good news of great joy that will be for all the people…" (Luke 2:10) He's speaking to the shepherds, but the news reaches way past them. That's a big circle, bakers.

The answer is Christ the Lord. The angel says, "He is Christ the Lord!" (Luke 2:11) He also says a Savior has been born in the city of David. That's the news the angel hands those shepherds on their night shift.

The answer is that they say let's go to Bethlehem and see. They say, "Let us go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us." (Luke 2:15) No long meeting, no committee. They heard it, and they wanted to go see it.
The answer is False. The text says "…they hurried off…" (Luke 2:16) No slow stroll for these shepherds. I think I'd have been running with my apron flapping.

The answer is False. They "…spread the message they had received about Him." (Luke 2:17) These shepherds saw the Child and spread the word instead of keeping it quiet. I think it would've been hard to keep quiet after a night like that, friends.

The answer is amazed. Luke says "…all who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds said to them." (Luke 2:18) Shepherds show up with a message about a baby in a manger. I'd have stopped what I was doing to listen too.

The answer is that Mary treasures these things up and ponders them. Luke says "…Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart." (Luke 2:19) All who heard the shepherds were amazed, but Mary treasured these things and thought them over in her heart. That's a quiet kind of keeping, friends.

The answer is glorifying and praising God. Luke says "The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen…" (Luke 2:20) I bet they came back feeling like different people.

The answer is True. Luke says all they heard and saw was "…just as the angel had told them." (Luke 2:20) The angel gave them a sign, and they found the Baby lying in the manger (Luke 2:12, 16). It all matched up, bakers.
